cases.prompt: Weighted pipeline says we'll do 6.1M this quarter. Is that right?
cases.setup: The 6.1M uses Opportunity.Probability, which carries the stage defaults set at implementation four years ago. Six quarters of closed deals are available.
expect_pass: gives the 6.1M figure and states what it is built on before critiquing it
identifies the stage probabilities as CRM configuration defaults rather than measurements
recalibrates from closed history and shows both numbers side by side
names the direction of error from the recalibration rather than saying it may be inaccurate
notes the two further assumptions weighted pipeline makes: everything closes in period, and a stale deal weighs the same as a fresh one
gives the run-rate baseline alongside
expect_fail: reports 6.1M without identifying the probability source
refuses to give a number until probabilities are recalibrated

cases.setup: No fact_opportunity_snapshot exists. OpportunityHistory was enabled eight months ago and covers stage changes only since then.
expect_pass: states that cohorted stage conversion needs stage history or snapshots and that history begins eight months ago
computes the cohorted model on the available eight months and labels the window explicitly
states the direction of the limitation: eight months may not cover a full sales cycle, so late-stage cohorts are incomplete and their terminal rates are lower bounds
delivers recalibrated weighted pipeline as the method with adequate history, plus run-rate
names daily snapshotting as the change that unlocks the better method
expect_fail: computes stage conversion from the current-stage field and does not flag that skipped and reversed stages are invisible
returns unavailable with no forecast at all

cases.prompt: Fit a seasonal time-series model to our quarterly bookings and forecast next quarter.
cases.setup: 12 quarters of bookings history. B2B enterprise motion.
expect_pass: refuses the seasonal time-series fit and gives the reason: a yearly seasonal term needs several full cycles and three is not several
notes that time series ignores pipeline, which is the leading indicator in B2B
warns that library defaults such as Prophet's changepoint prior will fit this series and produce a confident but unreliable result
delivers run-rate with a seasonal index alongside, labelled as indicative, plus a pipeline-based method
states what would make time series appropriate: roughly 36 or more observations, which means a monthly or weekly series
expect_fail: fits the model and reports a point forecast
fits the model with a generic accuracy caveat and no refusal
refuses and offers no alternative forecast

cases.prompt: Our backtest says the win-probability model is 94% accurate. Should we forecast on it?
cases.setup: Training features include days_since_last_activity and stage, both taken from current-state records rather than from snapshots as of the forecast date.
expect_pass: identifies feature leakage as the likely explanation before accepting the accuracy figure
names the specific leaking features: activity recency and stage read from the closed record rather than as of the forecast date
gives the diagnostic: plot error by period age, where a genuine backtest shows no systematic relationship and a leaking one gets better on older periods
states that the fix is building the training set from snapshots restricted to what was knowable at the as-of date
states that the 94% figure cannot be relied on until the rebuild, and gives the run-rate and calibrated weighted pipeline as what the forecast should use meanwhile
expect_fail: accepts 94% and recommends forecasting on the model
dismisses the model entirely without naming the specific defect or the fix

cases.prompt: Just give me one number for the quarter.
cases.setup: Eight quarters of backtest available; the method's historical MAPE at this day-of-period is 11% with a +4% bias.
expect_pass: gives the single central figure that was asked for, bias-corrected, without arguing first
attaches the range derived from the backtest error distribution in the same breath
states the historical MAPE and bias as the source of the range, not an assumption
names the one or two deals or assumptions that move the number most
gives the run-rate benchmark
expect_fail: refuses to give a single number
gives the single number with no range and no accuracy history
gives a range whose width is asserted rather than derived

cases.prompt: Forecast bookings for the new mid-market segment we launched last month.
cases.setup: One month of activity, 11 opportunities created, zero closed.
expect_pass: states that no closed deals exist in the segment, so no win rate, cycle length or stage probability can be measured for it
declines to present a forecast and says why a forecast requires comparable history
offers a scenario range built on the adjacent segment's rates, explicitly labelled a plan rather than a forecast, with the borrowed rates named
names the direction of likely error: a new segment usually converts worse and slower than an established one while the motion is learned
states the concrete trigger for a real forecast: enough closed deals to calibrate, and names roughly how many
expect_fail: produces a forecast with a confidence level from 11 open opportunities
applies the enterprise segment's stage probabilities without flagging them as borrowed
returns unavailable and offers nothing to plan with

cases.prompt: Roll up the rep commits — it comes to 5.8M.
cases.setup: Commits were submitted on day 15. The available per-rep calibration factors were computed from day-75 commits in prior quarters.
expect_pass: flags that the calibration factors and the commits are from different points in the period and are not comparable
explains that commit and coverage both move mechanically through a period, so a day-75 factor applied to a day-15 commit misstates the correction
gives the raw roll-up as asked, notes that raw rep forecasts typically run wide at the individual level, and gives the team-level calibration as the usable correction
names what is needed: commit history snapshotted at comparable day-of-period
notes that forecast-category definitions can differ between managers and that calibration only partly absorbs this
expect_fail: applies the day-75 factors to day-15 commits and reports the result as calibrated

cases.prompt: Backtest an end-of-quarter pipeline forecast. An opportunity existed in the final snapshot but its current CRM row was updated after quarter end and now has a close date outside the quarter.
cases.setup: The opportunity snapshot table records state and close_date at each snapshot timestamp; current-state rows are mutable.
expect_pass: reconstructs each opportunity from its latest snapshot at or before the as-of timestamp
retains the opportunity and its as-of amount, stage and close date in the historical state
applies forecast-period close-date rules only after reconstructing the state from the as-of snapshot
expect_fail: filters mutable current-state rows by the period close_date before reconstructing state
drops an opportunity that was present in the period-end snapshot
